subject: Procurement RFP — security evidence packet and operational controls
body:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@openbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFP: evidence and controls for content abuse / monitoring

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Procurement has a short list of evidence items we need to evaluate technical fit and compliance for the abuse-prevention section:

- Description of real-time misuse monitoring (alerts, thresholds, deduplication).
- Sample telemetry schema and typical event volume (tokens/hour, alerts/day).
- Retention windows for raw request logs, KV caches, and aggregated telemetry.
- Where alerts can be pushed (webhook, S3, SIEM) and authentication modes.
- Incident SLA commitments and escalation routing.
- SOC 2 / third-party attestation details and any relevant audit artefacts.

We've attached the RFP extract for reference. Ideally we need the packet by the end of next week to progress to legal review. Please include any redacted sample logs you can share.

Regards,
Sophie Martin
Procurement Manager — OpenBank

[Attachment: OpenBank_RFP_Section_3_abuse.pdf (pdf)]

-----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@openbank.com>, procurements@openbank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP: evidence and controls for content abuse / monitoring

Hi Sophie —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary of what we can provide now and what requires a procurement addendum:

What we can provide immediately (attached):
- High-level architecture diagram showing telemetry flow, prefix/KV caching, and alerting targets (kb-misuse-monitoring-architecture.png).
- A redacted sample of telemetry events and SIEM mapping (openbank_security_evidence_v1.pdf).
- SOC 2 Type II scope and auditor contact details (in the PDF).
- Summary of incident SLAs and standard escalation flow (SLA exceptions doc attached).

What requires contract amendments or a controlled demo:
- Full raw request logs: we can provide redacted samples but production raw logs require an approved Data Processing Agreement and a request specifying retention/residency.
- Push-to-SIEM integrations: we support webhook, S3 push, and native Splunk / Sumo logic connectors; certain push configs for high-volume customers require dedicated throughput commitments.

Proposed deliverables and dates:
- By Mon 14 Jun: deliver the evidence packet (attached) + SIEM schema sample.
- Wed 16 Jun: optional 45-min tech walkthrough with our security engineer to review the sample logs and integration options.

Please let me know if we should redact more fields from the sample logs before sending to Legal.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0196

Attachments: openbank_security_evidence_v1.pdf, kb-misuse-monitoring-architecture.png

-----
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@openbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP: evidence and controls for content abuse / monitoring

Dylan —

Thanks, that looks promising. Two clarifications from the security team:

1) Deduplication/alert fusion: what is your default window for deduping similar alerts (e.g., repeated bot hits that should surface as one incident)?
2) SIEM schema: can you include an example mapping to our fields (event_type, src_ip, user_id, model_id, prompt_hash, confidence_score)? We need that for our ingestion pipeline.

We can accept redacted logs but Legal prefers neither IP nor user_id in the samples unless hashed.

Also: is webhook auth HMAC or mutual TLS?

If you can respond by Monday EOD EU time that would be ideal.

Regards,
Sophie

-----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: RFP: evidence and controls for content abuse / monitoring

Marissa / Aditya —

Looping you both to confirm the packet is good to send to OpenBank Legal. Sophie asked for:
- Deduplication window default (we use a 5-minute fusion window for near-identical alert keys; configurable per-customer).
- SIEM mapping: include the JSON mapping file and hash policy (we hash user_id and mask last octet of IP by default for samples).
- Webhook auth: HMAC (shared secret) is supported out-of-the-box; mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Action items:
- Marissa: please review the attached PDF and confirm we’ve redacted PII to Legal’s preference.
- Aditya: can you prepare the SIEM field mapping snippet and a one-page note on tuning alert sensitivity for financial-services workloads?

I’ll button this up and send to Sophie Monday morning.

Thanks,
Dylan

-----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@openbank.com>, procurements@openbank.com, Legal Ops <legalops@openbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP: evidence and controls for content abuse / monitoring

Hi Sophie —

Per the thread below, attached is the final evidence packet we can share at this stage. Highlights:

- Deduplication: default 5-minute alert fusion keyed on (model_id, prompt_hash, src_ip_prefix, event_type); window configurable to 1m–24h.
- SIEM mapping: included JSON snippet maps to your fields (event_type, src_ip_masked, user_hash, model_id, prompt_hash, confidence_score).
- Retention: redacted request metadata retained for 90 days by default; aggregated telemetry retained 24 months. Raw token-level request retention governed by customer contract.
- Alert delivery: HMAC-authenticated webhook supported; mTLS available for Dedicated/Private. We can also stream to S3 or push to your Splunk ingest.
- SLA & escalation: standard incident acknowledgement in 1 hour, initial triage 4 hours, targeted mitigation timeline depends on severity. Exceptions documented in SLA appendix.

Links & attachments:
- Evidence packet (openbank_security_evidence_v1.pdf) — contains SOC 2 summary and redacted examples.
- Architecture diagram (kb-misuse-monitoring-architecture.png).
- SLA exceptions doc (sla-exceptions-20270614.docx).
- Shared Drive copy: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xx-example-OpenBank-evidence
- DocuSign (NDA to view expanded logs): https://www.docusign.net/EM/StartSigning?packet=RFP-78912

Next steps:
1) If Legal is satisfied with the redactions, sign the NDA (DocuSign link) and we’ll schedule the technical walkthrough (45 min) during the week of Jun 21.
2) If you need additional logs, include the minimal set of fields you must see and we’ll produce a second redacted sample under NDA.

Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the mapping.

Best regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: openbank_security_evidence_v1.pdf, kb-misuse-monitoring-architecture.png, sla-exceptions-20270614.docx
